_link.title: I can distinguish between the mechanism of a catalyst and that of a temperature increase

toLevel2.stem: How does a catalyst increase the rate of a reaction?
distractors: By increasing particle kinetic energy
By raising the activation energy
By increasing the temperature

toLevel2.stem: How does a temperature increase speed up a reaction?
toLevel2.answer: By giving particles more kinetic energy to exceed the activation energy
distractors: By lowering the activation energy of the reaction
By providing an alternative reaction pathway
By reducing the number of collisions per second

toLevel2.stem: What is the key difference between how a catalyst and a temperature increase affect rate?
toLevel2.answer: A catalyst lowers Ea; temperature increases particle energy
distractors: A catalyst increases Ea; temperature decreases particle energy
Both lower Ea but by different amounts
Both increase particle energy but by different amounts

toLevel2.stem: Does a temperature increase change the activation energy of a reaction?
toLevel2.answer: No, the activation energy remains unchanged
distractors: Yes, it lowers the activation energy
Yes, it raises the activation energy
Yes, it eliminates the activation energy

toLevel2.stem: Does a catalyst increase the kinetic energy of particles?
distractors: Yes, it gives particles more kinetic energy
Yes, it doubles the kinetic energy of every particle
Yes, it raises the average speed of particles

toLevel2.stem: A catalyst lowers the activation energy, while a temperature increase gives particles more kinetic energy.
distractors: False

toLevel2.stem: Both a catalyst and a temperature increase work by lowering the activation energy of a reaction.
distractors: True

toLevel3.stem: Using the exam analogy, how does a catalyst work compared to a temperature increase?
toLevel3.answer: A catalyst lowers the pass mark; a temperature increase helps students score higher
distractors: A catalyst helps students score higher; a temperature increase lowers the pass mark
Both lower the pass mark but by different amounts
Both help students score higher but through different methods

toLevel3.stem: Why do a catalyst and a temperature increase both result in more successful collisions, despite working differently?
toLevel3.answer: Both increase the proportion of particles that meet or exceed the energy threshold
distractors: Both lower the activation energy of the reaction by the same amount
Both increase the speed of every particle in exactly the same way
Both change the orientation of particles to improve collision success

toLevel3.stem: Why is it important to distinguish between the mechanisms of a catalyst and a temperature increase?
toLevel3.answer: They have different practical applications and are assessed differently in exams
distractors: They are identical mechanisms and there is no real distinction needed
Only temperature is useful in practice; catalysts have no applications
Only catalysts are useful in practice; temperature changes are impractical

toLevel3.stem: A catalyst allows more particles to exceed the activation energy without gaining extra energy. How is this possible?
toLevel3.answer: The catalyst lowers the threshold so existing particle energies are now sufficient
distractors: The catalyst secretly adds energy to each particle without changing temperature
The catalyst removes the need for collisions to occur between particles
The catalyst changes the orientation of all particles to the correct alignment

toLevel3.stem: On a Maxwell-Boltzmann diagram, how would you show the difference between a catalyst and a temperature increase?
toLevel3.answer: A catalyst moves the Ea line left; a temperature increase changes the curve shape
distractors: Both move the Ea line to the left by different amounts
Both change the curve shape in the same direction
A catalyst changes the curve shape; a temperature increase moves the Ea line

toLevel3.stem: Why might a catalyst be preferred over a temperature increase in an industrial process?
toLevel3.answer: A catalyst avoids the energy cost and risks of heating to high temperatures
distractors: A catalyst always produces more product than a temperature increase
A temperature increase cannot speed up any industrial reaction
A catalyst increases the energy of particles more effectively than heat

toLevel3.stem: A catalyst and a temperature increase both result in more particles exceeding the activation energy, but by different mechanisms.
distractors: False

toLevel4.stem: A student draws a Maxwell-Boltzmann diagram. To show the effect of a catalyst, they shift the curve to the right. What correction is needed?
toLevel4.answer: The curve should stay the same; only the Ea line should move to the left
distractors: The curve should shift even further to the right than drawn
The curve should shift to the left instead of to the right
Both the curve and the Ea line should shift to the right

toLevel4.stem: A student draws two Maxwell-Boltzmann diagrams: one showing the effect of a catalyst and one showing the effect of a temperature increase. In the catalyst diagram, the student changes the curve shape. What error did they make?
toLevel4.answer: The catalyst diagram should show the same curve with only the Ea line moved
distractors: The temperature diagram should show the same curve with only the Ea line moved
Both diagrams should show changed curve shapes with identical Ea lines
Neither diagram should show any changes to the curve or the Ea line

toLevel4.stem: In the Haber process, an iron catalyst is used rather than simply heating the reaction mixture to a very high temperature. Using the distinction between mechanisms, why?
toLevel4.answer: The catalyst lowers Ea without requiring extreme heating, saving energy and avoiding side reactions
distractors: The iron catalyst increases the kinetic energy of particles more than heat would
The iron catalyst raises the temperature of the mixture automatically
Heating cannot increase rate in the Haber process under any conditions

toLevel4.stem: A reaction proceeds slowly at room temperature. A student has two options: add a catalyst or heat the mixture. If both achieve the same rate increase, which option uses less energy input?
toLevel4.answer: Adding a catalyst, because it does not require continuous energy to maintain higher temperature
distractors: Heating the mixture, because temperature changes are always more energy-efficient
Both options use exactly the same amount of energy for the same rate increase
Adding a catalyst uses more energy because the catalyst must be manufactured

toLevel4.stem: A student explains: 'A catalyst works by heating the reaction mixture.' Using the distinction between mechanisms, correct this statement.
toLevel4.answer: A catalyst provides an alternative pathway with lower Ea; it does not heat the mixture
distractors: The statement is correct — catalysts generate heat to speed up reactions
A catalyst works by cooling the reaction mixture to lower the Ea
A catalyst works by removing particles that would slow down the reaction

toLevel4.stem: A student uses the pass-mark analogy to explain catalysis. They say: 'A catalyst is like giving students extra tutoring to improve their scores.' Is this correct?
toLevel4.answer: No — extra tutoring is the temperature analogy; a catalyst is like lowering the pass mark
distractors: Yes — extra tutoring is the correct analogy for how catalysts work
No — the pass-mark analogy does not apply to catalysis at all
Yes — both analogies represent the same mechanism correctly

toLevel4.stem: In biological systems, enzymes (biological catalysts) allow reactions to proceed at body temperature. Using the distinction between mechanisms, why don't cells simply increase temperature?
toLevel4.answer: High temperatures would denature proteins and damage cells; enzymes lower Ea instead
distractors: Cells cannot absorb heat from the environment under any circumstances
Temperature increases would lower the Ea too much, making reactions uncontrollable
Enzymes increase the kinetic energy of particles more efficiently than heat

toLevel5.stem: A student says: 'Both a catalyst and temperature increase lead to more successful collisions, so they must work the same way.' Analyze this reasoning.
toLevel5.answer: The outcome is similar but the mechanisms differ: catalyst lowers Ea, temperature raises particle energy
distractors: The reasoning is correct — same outcome means same mechanism
The reasoning is wrong because only temperature increases successful collisions
The reasoning is wrong because only catalysts increase successful collisions

toLevel5.stem: A student writes: 'A catalyst is always better than a temperature increase for speeding up reactions.' Evaluate this claim.
toLevel5.answer: Not always — some reactions lack a suitable catalyst, and temperature may be the only practical option
distractors: Correct — catalysts are always more effective and cheaper than heating
Incorrect — temperature increases are always superior to catalysts
Correct — catalysts work for every reaction and temperature never does

toLevel5.stem: On a Maxwell-Boltzmann diagram, both a catalyst and a temperature increase result in a larger shaded area beyond Ea. How can you tell which diagram shows which effect?
toLevel5.answer: If the curve shape changed, it is temperature; if only the Ea line moved, it is a catalyst
distractors: Both effects look identical on a Maxwell-Boltzmann diagram
If the area increased, it must be a catalyst; if it decreased, it is temperature
The catalyst diagram always shows a larger area than the temperature diagram

toLevel5.stem: A peer claims: 'If a catalyst lowers the activation energy enough, every collision will result in a reaction.' Evaluate this claim.
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect — particles still need correct orientation regardless of how low Ea becomes
distractors: Correct — zero activation energy means every collision is successful
Incorrect — catalysts can never lower Ea enough to have any measurable effect
Correct — orientation is only needed when Ea is high, not when it is low

toLevel5.stem: In an industrial process, both a catalyst and elevated temperature are used simultaneously. How do their effects combine on a Maxwell-Boltzmann diagram?
toLevel5.answer: The curve shifts right and broadens (temperature) while the Ea line moves left (catalyst)
distractors: Both effects move the Ea line to the left by different amounts
Both effects shift the curve to the right by different amounts
The effects cancel each other out and the diagram remains unchanged

toLevel5.stem: A student argues: 'Since a catalyst is not consumed, it provides free energy to the reaction.' Is this reasoning valid?
toLevel5.answer: No — a catalyst does not provide energy; it lowers the energy threshold via an alternative pathway
distractors: Yes — the catalyst's regeneration releases energy that drives the reaction forward
No — the catalyst is consumed and must be replaced after each reaction cycle
Yes — not being consumed means the catalyst transfers its energy to particles

toLevel5.stem: Why is the distinction between catalyst and temperature mechanisms important for biological systems?
toLevel5.answer: Organisms use enzymes to lower Ea because they cannot survive the high temperatures needed otherwise
distractors: Organisms prefer temperature increases because enzymes are too expensive to produce
The distinction is not important for biological systems since both methods are equivalent
Organisms use temperature increases exclusively because enzymes cannot lower Ea

toLevel5.stem: A student claims that using a catalyst and increasing temperature together would not further increase rate beyond what either achieves alone. Is this valid?
toLevel5.answer: No — the effects are complementary and using both can increase rate beyond either alone
distractors: Yes — the effects cancel each other out when used simultaneously
Yes — once Ea is lowered by a catalyst, temperature has no further effect
No — but only because the catalyst is destroyed at high temperatures
